children.title: Cycle 5 · Advancing Intelligent Disobedience and Reasoning Blind Spot Frameworks

detail.title: Advancing Intelligent Disobedience and Reasoning Blind Spot Frameworks
detail.summary: This cycle progresses the research into intelligent disobedience in shared autonomy and LLM reasoning blind spots. We are actively expanding the evidentiary base for intelligent disobedience beyond the current single-source limitation, and initiating deeper technical analysis into the Thought Space Explorer (TSE) framework to evaluate its efficacy in navigating epistemic blind spots.

children.title: Cycle 4 · LLM Reasoning Blind Spots and Knowledge Gaps

detail.title: LLM Reasoning Blind Spots and Knowledge Gaps
detail.summary: Current LLM reasoning research distinguishes between procedural blind spots (unexplored search spaces in reasoning chains) and epistemic knowledge gaps (inability to recognize unknowns). Frameworks like Thought Space Explorer (TSE) address procedural blind spots through node-based path expansion, while knowledge gap awareness research focuses on meta-cognitive mechanisms like uncertainty quantification and reflective prompting.

detail.summary: This research entry explores the formalization of 'intelligent disobedience'—a safety-critical behavior where agents must override human commands to prevent harm—using the Intelligent Disobedience Game (IDG) as a foundational framework.
